subtype: Child hiding pain to avoid fuss [Actor]
passage: Last month my back tooth hurt for days, and I didn't tell anyone. I was scared the dentist would give me an injection. So I chewed on one side and said I wasn't hungry. When my sister Sarika asked to play carrom, I shouted, "Leave me alone!" and slammed the door. Ammi found me holding my cheek. "Asif, what's hurting?" I cried and told her. She wasn't angry. She hugged me and took me to the dentist the next day. The dentist explained everything first, and it wasn't as bad as I thought. I said sorry to Sarika.

qa.q: What did Asif shout when Sarika asked to play carrom?
Why did Asif keep the toothache secret?
qa.a: Asif was scared the dentist would give an injection, so fear made hiding the pain feel safer.

qa.q: What turned things around, and what could Asif do next time?
qa.a: Telling Ammi, who hugged Asif and arranged the dentist; next time, saying something early would end the pain sooner.

qa.q: How might Sarika have felt when the door slammed?
qa.a: Sarika was probably hurt and confused, not knowing the shouting came from a sore tooth.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild hiding a sore tooth out of fear of injections, with the pain leaking out as withdrawal and temper until an adult helps.

subtype: Child hiding pain to avoid fuss [Actor]
passage:
Class teacher's note, Class Three.
Chaitanya is usually chatty and busy, but for two days he has sat curled at his desk, snapping "I'm fine!" when asked anything. Today he refused to go out at break and pushed his tiffin away. At the end of break I sat beside him and said he wasn't in trouble. He whispered that his tummy had been hurting, but he hadn't told anyone because he didn't want to miss the school trip or make his mother worried. I told him telling a grown-up was the right thing, and that we would sort out the trip together. I took him to the school nurse, then phoned his mother, who came to collect him that afternoon to see their doctor. Noor (class teacher)

qa.q: What was Chaitanya worried about when he hid his tummy ache?
qa.a: He was anxious about missing the school trip and about making his mother worried, so he kept the pain to himself.

qa.q: Which of Noor's steps helped most, and why?
qa.a: Sitting with him, saying he was not in trouble and reassuring him about the trip, which made it safe to talk; then the nurse and a call home the same day.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya's mother feel after the call?
qa.a: She would likely be concerned but relieved that the teacher noticed and called, so he could see their doctor that day.

grounding: Illustrates a child hiding a tummy ache to avoid missing a trip or worrying a parent, with the pain showing as withdrawal and short temper.
